claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1 show an Xbox console and controller.
Photo 1 shows one black wireless controller.
No games or disc cases are shown in the report.
The power supply is not shown and its functionality cannot be tested remotely.

risks.risk: Console may not power on at all (internal failure beyond the adaptor).
risks.proof: A video showing the console booting to the home dashboard with a working power supply.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty or unable to read discs.
risks.proof: A video of a game disc being inserted, recognized, and launched.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken disc drive

risks.risk: The controller may have stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used in the 'Test Controller' menu in settings.

risks.risk: Internal storage might be the lower 500GB capacity rather than 1TB.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the 'Storage' section in the system settings.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and reaching the dashboard.
Video of a disc being inserted and the game loading.
Screenshot of the system settings showing storage capacity.
Photos of the 6 games mentioned by the seller.
Photo of the power adaptor to see physical damage.
response.reason: The item is identified as an original Xbox One; however, due to the admitted power issue and lack of functional proof, it must be priced as a non-working unit for parts.
